title: o_e (silent e)
parentNote: The silent e now does its trick to an o: hop becomes hope, not becomes note, rod becomes rode. The idea is two days old already, so the new part is only the vowel — but the old habit is strong and the commonest slip is reading straight past the e, so hope comes out as hop. Write hop, read it together, then add an e in a different colour and read it again; four or five pairs teach it faster than any explaining. The other slip is sounding the e out — "hoh-puh" — so when you point, keep the p and the e covered as one lump and let the o say its name in the middle. If your child asks about come or gone, English simply breaks its own rule in those two; say so plainly and move on.

activities.mouthCue: Lips pushed forward into a round o — the same shape as yesterday, held a little longer.
activities.prompt: The e on the end says nothing. It reaches back over the m and tells the o to say its own name.
Three ways of writing an o. Which one has a silent e waiting at the end?
Two of these have a gap with a silent e after it. Only one makes an o sound.
Three sounds, not four. The m and the e go together and the e stays quiet.
Same start as home. Only the lump at the end is different.
Two sounds at the front this time, and the quiet e still at the back.
The longest one. Front blend, o saying its name, then ke.
Same three letters at the front. One of them has the silent e on the end.
Listen to the middle sound. Short o, or the o saying its name?
Two of these have the silent e. The sound just before it decides which.
Both say the o sound. One has a team of two letters and one has a silent e on the end.

activities.text: The doe goes up the slope, and Joe rode home.
A mole dug a hole in the path and hid in it.
Meg broke the cone, and Joe did not help!

activities.title: The mole and the hole
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Joe rode up the slope with Meg on a red bike.
A mole had dug a big hole in the path.
The bike hit the hole and broke!
Meg got a rope and did tug the bike home.
The mole sat up on a stone and did grin.
It did not help. It did munch the rope.

questions.prompt: Joe rode up the slope on ...
Meg did tug the bike home with ...
